ai.title: Add /connect:claude command for OAuth integration
ai.summary: CLI adds /connect:claude command enabling Claude subscription OAuth via browser flow. New components handle auth code exchange, quota polling, and status display. Shared constants and SDK model-provider updated to support Claude OAuth. BottomStatusLine shows quota percentage and reset time when connected.

eli5.text: If you pay for Claude as a subscriber, you can now connect your account inside the assistant by typing a special command, which opens your web browser so you can log in and approve the connection. Once connected, a status line appears below the input box showing your remaining usage quota and when it resets. The connection uses an OAuth browser flow, exchanging a code for tokens and polling for quota data behind the scenes.

ai.title: Replace TanStack Query with custom activity-aware query hook in CLI
ai.summary: Introduced `useActivityQuery` and `activityTracker` to replace `@tanstack/react-query` in the CLI, resolving terminal polling instability. The new singleton tracker detects user inactivity to pause background refetches, while `useUsageQuery` and `useClaudeQuotaQuery` now leverage this mechanism for efficient credit polling. Scope includes `cli/src/hooks/use-activity-query.ts`, `cli/src/utils/activity-tracker.ts`, and updated consumers in `chat.tsx` and banner components. Manual `setInterval` polling hacks in `usage-banner.tsx` were removed in favor of `refetchInterval` managed by the activity state.

eli5.text: When you're not typing or actively using the terminal, the assistant now pauses background checks for things like your remaining credits instead of repeatedly polling the server while idle. When you start interacting again, it picks up where it left off. Previously, these background checks kept running even when you stepped away, which could become unreliable in terminal sessions.

ai.title: Color-code CLI subscription usage
ai.summary: Bottom status line now applies conditional coloring to remaining subscription percentage. Thresholds set at <=10% (error) and <=25% (warning), defaulting to muted otherwise. Change isolated to cli/src/components/bottom-status-line.tsx. Purely visual; no logic or data flow alterations.

eli5.text: The bottom status line in the CLI now displays your subscription usage percentage in color, red when at or below 10% remaining, yellow at or below 25%, and muted otherwise, providing a visual cue for how much of your subscription capacity is available. This purely visual change affects anyone running the CLI and viewing the bottom status bar, and you would notice the percentage immediately changing color when your remaining subscription approaches the warning or error thresholds.

ai.title: Add /buy-credits slash command
ai.summary: New `/buy-credits` command added to CLI command registry and slash command list. Opens `WEBSITE_URL + '/profile?tab=usage'` in browser via `open` package. Command excluded from input history. Files: `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts`, `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts`.

eli5.text: You can now type /buy-credits in the command-line tool to open your account's usage page in your web browser, where you can add more credits to your subscription. The command appears in the list of slash commands you can use, and it won't be saved in your conversation history. This just went live today as part of a minor update.

ai.title: Fix useActivityQuery polling interval reset
ai.summary: The `useActivityQuery` hook now stores `queryFn` in a ref to prevent polling interval resets caused by inline function references changing on every render. This fixes a bug where the `doFetch` dependency array included `queryFn`, causing `useCallback` to recreate the fetch logic frequently and interrupt background polling. The change is isolated to `cli/src/hooks/use-activity-query.ts`. `isEntryStale` was also exported to facilitate testing of the cache staleness logic.

eli5.text: If you use the CLI tool to check your activity, background refreshes no longer get interrupted. Previously a small part of how the tool remembers what to fetch changed on every screen update, which silently restarted the timed fetch loop and could stall live data. That part now stays put so polling keeps its schedule. The change is live today.

ai.title: Include HTTP status in ads API logs
ai.summary: web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts now logs response.status across all Gravity API paths. Error branch returns 500 with getErrorObject(error) instead of silent 200. Scope limited to ads API handler.

eli5.text: When the system fetches an ad on your behalf and the ad service responds, it now records the exact HTTP status code (like 200, 404, 500) in its logs instead of leaving a generic entry. For you, that means if something goes wrong while loading an ad, the log will clearly show the specific error code the ad service returned, making problems faster to diagnose. The change is live now and affects all ad fetches handled by the ads endpoint.

ai.summary: The codebuff package version in cli/release/package.json was bumped from 1.0.574, shipping no functional code changes of its own. This release packages prior day work: the /buy-credits slash command (cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts, cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts), the useActivityQuery polling interval reset fix (cli/src/hooks/use-activity-query.ts), and HTTP status logging in the ads API path (web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts). Consumers will see the updated version string in package resolution and CLI startup output.

eli5.text: This release adds a new `/buy-credits` slash command that opens your browser directly to the usage page where you can purchase additional compute credits, making it faster to top up your account when you run low. The background activity tracking that keeps your session info fresh has been fixed so it now polls at a steady interval instead of restarting constantly, which reduces unnecessary processing and keeps your activity updates more reliable. For users who see sponsored ads in the app, error reporting for ad delivery has been improved, so problems are now logged properly with the correct HTTP status codes and return clearer error responses instead of silent successes. Upgrading gives you quicker access to paid features, smoother background syncing, and more accurate ad-related diagnostics behind the scenes.

ai.title: Gravity ads send last 3 user messages
ai.summary: The `useGravityAd` hook in `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` now filters `adMessages` to include only the last three user messages, stripping `<user_message>` tags, before sending them to the `/api/v1/ads` endpoint. This change reduces the payload size sent to the ad service by excluding assistant responses and older history. The logging statement also reflects this filtered set.

eli5.text: When the assistant looks for ads to show you in the terminal, it now sends only your last three messages instead of the entire conversation back and forth. This means the ad service gets less information about your chat, focusing just on what you recently asked, which keeps the data payload smaller. If you were checking network traffic you'd see fewer messages being transmitted in those ad requests.
